noun.label: Noun
noun.plain: A naming word: a person, place, thing or idea, like “book”, “mercy”, “day”. In Arabic it also covers many words English treats differently, such as describing words and words like “before” and “after”.
noun.short: a naming word for a person, thing or idea

proper.label: Proper noun
proper.plain: The name of one particular person, place or being, like Allah, Mūsā (Moses) or Makkah.
proper.short: a name of one particular person or place

verb.label: Verb
verb.plain: An action or happening word, like “said”, “believe”, “go!”. An Arabic verb also carries who does it (he, they, you…) and when, so one verb can be a whole small sentence, like “they said”.
verb.short: an action word: something done or happening

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: verbs, subjects and objects

pronoun.label: Pronoun
pronoun.plain: A stand-in for a noun, so it need not be repeated: “he, it, his, them, you, we”. In Arabic most pronouns are small endings joined to another word, like “his” on “book” to make “his book”.
pronoun.short: a stand-in for a noun: he, it, his, them

adjective.label: Adjective
adjective.plain: A describing word: it tells you what something is like, “merciful”, “great”, “straight”. In Arabic it comes after the noun it describes and matches it, so “the path, the straight” means “the straight path”.
adjective.short: a describing word: what something is like

preposition.label: Preposition
preposition.plain: A small word that places one thing in relation to another: “in, on, from, to, with, by”. The noun after it takes the genitive ending (usually -i).
preposition.short: a small word like “in, from, to, with”

conjunction.label: Conjunction
conjunction.plain: A joining word: it links words or sentences, “and”, “then”, “or”. In Arabic “and” (وَ) and “then” (فَ) are written joined to the next word.

determiner.label: Determiner (the)
determiner.plain: The word “the”. In Arabic it is the prefix al- (الـ) written at the front of the noun: الْكِتَاب “the book”.
determiner.short: “the”: the prefix al- on a noun

negation.label: Negation
negation.plain: The colour for words that say “not” or “do not”: negative particles like لَا and مَا, and words that forbid or refuse. Tap a word’s own label to see which kind it is.
negation.short: a word that says “not” or “do not”

particle.label: Particle
particle.plain: A small helper word that never changes form. It doesn’t name a thing or an action; it links words or shades the meaning, like “and”, “not”, “in”, “then”, “indeed”.
particle.short: a small helper word that links or shades meaning

relative.label: Relative noun
relative.plain: A word meaning “who”, “what” or “that which”. It points back to someone or something and introduces a description of it: “those who believed”, “what you worship”.
relative.short: “who / what / that which”: introduces a description

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the subordinate clause

time-adverb.label: Time adverb
time-adverb.plain: A word saying when something happens: “when”, “then”, “the day”, “before”.
time-adverb.short: a word saying when: “when, the day, before”

place-adverb.label: Place adverb
place-adverb.plain: A word saying where something is: “with”, “there”, “between”, “under”.
place-adverb.short: a word saying where: “with, between, under”

active-participle.label: Active participle
active-participle.plain: A noun made from a verb that names the one who does the action: from “believe” comes مُؤْمِن “a believer, one who believes”; from “create” comes خَالِق “Creator”. It can often be read as “-er” or “-ing”.
active-participle.short: the one who does the action: “believer, doer”

passive-participle.label: Passive participle
passive-participle.plain: A noun made from a verb that names the one the action is done to: from “know” comes مَعْلُوم “known”. It is like English “-ed”.
passive-participle.short: the one the action is done to: “known, written”

masdar.label: Verbal noun (masdar)
masdar.plain: The name of an action itself, like English “-ing” or “-tion”: from “praise” comes حَمْد “praise”; from “believe” comes إِيمَان “belief, believing”.
masdar.short: the name of an action: “praise, belief, going”

verb-noun.label: Verbal noun
verb-noun.plain: A word that acts like a verb or an exclamation but never changes form like one: أُفٍّ “ugh!”, or one meaning “come!” or “how far!”.
verb-noun.short: an exclamation that acts like a verb: “ugh!”, “come!”

initials.label: Quranic initials
initials.plain: Separate letters that open some surahs, read letter by letter, like الٓمٓ “alif lām mīm”. Their meaning is not explained in the Qur’an, so they are left untranslated.
initials.short: opening letters of a surah, read one by one

negative.label: Negative particle
negative.plain: A word that makes something negative: “not”. The common ones are لَا, مَا, لَمْ, لَنْ and إِنْ (when it means “not”).

interrogative.label: Interrogative particle
interrogative.plain: A question word, used to ask: “is…?”, “do…?”, “what?”, “how?”. أَ at the front of a sentence turns it into a yes-or-no question.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the particle alif

supplemental.label: Supplemental particle
supplemental.plain: A small added word that keeps the sentence flowing and often adds emphasis, but does not change its basic meaning, so translations often leave it out or render it lightly (“so”, “then”, “indeed”).
supplemental.short: a small added word for flow or emphasis

resumption.label: Resumption particle
resumption.plain: “And” or “so” at the start of a new sentence: it carries the passage on to a fresh statement rather than joining two words together. Usually وَ or فَ.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the particle fa

accusative.label: Accusative particle
accusative.plain: A small word like إِنَّ “indeed”, أَنَّ “that” or لَعَلَّ “perhaps” that changes the ending of the word after it to the accusative (usually -a).
accusative.short: “indeed / that”, setting the next ending to -a

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the particle inna

subordinating.label: Subordinating conjunction
subordinating.plain: A word like أَنْ “that, to” or مَا “what, as” that turns the clause after it into one part of a bigger sentence: “that you fast” works like the noun “your fasting”.
subordinating.short: “that / to”: makes a clause part of the sentence

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the subordinate clause

emphasis.label: Emphasis (lām)
emphasis.plain: The letter لَ joined to a word to stress it: “surely, certainly”.

conditional.label: Conditional particle
conditional.plain: “If” or “whenever”: it sets a condition, and the rest of the sentence says what follows from it.

restriction.label: Restriction particle
restriction.plain: “Only” or “none but”: it limits a statement to one thing. Often إِلَّا after a “not”: مَا … إِلَّا “nothing but…”.
restriction.short: “only / none but”: limits to one thing

certainty.label: Particle of certainty
certainty.plain: قَدْ before a past verb: “certainly, indeed, already”.

future.label: Future particle
future.plain: سَـ or سَوْفَ before a present verb: “will”.

vocative.label: Vocative particle
vocative.plain: A calling word, used to address someone: “O…!”.

prohibition.label: Prohibition particle
prohibition.plain: لَا telling someone not to do something: “do not”. The verb after it takes the jussive form.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the subjunctive and jussive moods

answer.label: Answer particle
answer.plain: A word that answers: “yes” or “no”, like بَلَىٰ “yes indeed” and نَعَمْ “yes”.

inceptive.label: Inceptive particle
inceptive.plain: A word that opens a new statement, such as حَتَّىٰ “until, then at last” or بَلْ “rather”, when what follows stands as its own sentence.
inceptive.short: opens a new statement: “until, then at last”

circumstantial.label: Circumstantial particle
circumstantial.plain: وَ meaning “while”: it introduces the situation in which something happens.

causal.label: Causal particle
causal.plain: فَ meaning “so that, lest”: it gives a reason or a result that hangs on what came before.
causal.short: “so that”: gives a cause or result

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the particle fa

purpose.label: Purpose particle (lām)
purpose.plain: The letter لِ before a verb, meaning “so that” or “in order to”.

retraction.label: Retraction particle
retraction.plain: A turning word: بَلْ “nay, rather” sets aside what came before for something truer, and لَٰكِنْ “but” corrects or qualifies it. (The corpus calls بَلْ a retraction and لَٰكِنْ an amendment; the app shows both under this one label.)

aversion.label: Aversion particle
aversion.plain: كَلَّا: a firm “No!” or “By no means!” that rejects what was just said or thought.

exceptive.label: Exceptive particle
exceptive.plain: “Except” or “but not”: it takes one thing out of a group.
exceptive.short: “except”: leaves one out of a group

exhortation.label: Exhortation particle
exhortation.plain: لَوْلَا or لَوْمَا meaning “why not…?” or “if only…”: it urges or reproaches.

surprise.label: Surprise particle
surprise.plain: إِذَا meaning “and behold!” or “suddenly”: something unexpected happens at once.

detail.label: Detail particle
detail.plain: أَمَّا “as for…” or إِمَّا “either… or”: it sets out cases one by one.

explanatory.label: Explanatory particle
explanatory.plain: أَنْ meaning “that is” or “namely”: it spells out the words of what was said, revealed or commanded.

equalization.label: Equalization particle
equalization.plain: أَ meaning “whether”, after words like “it is the same”: “it is the same whether… or…”.
equalization.short: “whether… or”: it is the same either way

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the particle alif

comitative.label: Comitative (wāw)
comitative.plain: وَ meaning “along with, together with” rather than a plain “and”.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the comitative object

result.label: Result particle
result.plain: فَ meaning “then”, opening what follows from an “if”: “if you do this, then…”.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the particle fa

preventive.label: Preventive particle
preventive.plain: A small مَا joined to a word like إِنَّ, which stops that word changing the ending of the next one. Together, إِنَّمَا often means “only”.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the particle inna

attention.label: Attention particle
attention.plain: A word that calls for attention: أَلَا “Behold! Truly!”, and the هَا in هَٰذَا “this” or يَا أَيُّهَا “O you”.

distance.label: Distance particle
distance.plain: The لِ inside ذَٰلِكَ “that” and تِلْكَ: it shows the thing pointed at is further away, “that” rather than “this”.

address.label: Address particle
address.plain: The كَ at the end of ذَٰلِكَ “that” and similar words: it faces the person spoken to. It is not “you” or “your” in the meaning; it changes to كُمْ when a group is addressed.
address.short: the k in ذَٰلِكَ, facing the listener

nominative.label: nominative
nominative.plain: The ending (usually -u) a noun has when it is the subject, the one doing or being something.

accusative-case.label: accusative
accusative-case.plain: The ending (usually -a) a noun has when it is the object, the one something is done to, or after words like إِنَّ.

genitive.label: genitive
genitive.plain: The ending (usually -i) a noun has after a preposition (“in, from, to”) or as the “of” part of a pair, like “the name of Allah”.

indefinite.label: indefinite
indefinite.plain: “A” or “an” rather than “the”: a noun not pointing to one particular thing. It usually ends in -n: كِتَابٌ “a book”.

masculine.label: masculine
masculine.plain: Every Arabic noun, and every verb and adjective that goes with it, is grammatically masculine or feminine. Masculine is the default form: “he”.

feminine.label: feminine
feminine.plain: The grammatically feminine form, often marked by ـة or ـت: “she”. Things as well as people can be feminine, so it is a grammar class, not always about being female.

dual.label: dual
dual.plain: Exactly two. Arabic has its own form for a pair, usually ending -āni or -ayni.

plural.label: plural
plural.plain: Three or more, since Arabic has a separate form for two.

person2.label: 2nd person
person2.plain: The one spoken to: “you”. Arabic has different “you” forms for a man, a woman, two people and a group.

person3.label: 3rd person
person3.plain: The one spoken about: “he, she, it, they”.
person3.short: the one spoken about: “he, she, they”

perfect.label: perfect
perfect.plain: The verb form for a finished action, mostly read as past: قَالَ “he said”. Its “who” is shown by an ending.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: verbs, subjects and objects

imperfect.label: imperfect
imperfect.plain: The verb form for an action not yet finished, read as present or future: يَقُولُ “he says, he will say”. Its “who” is shown by a prefix, like يَـ “he” or نَـ “we”.
imperfect.short: an unfinished action: present or future

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: verbs, subjects and objects

imperative.label: imperative
imperative.plain: The verb form for a command or request: “do!”, “say!”, “guide us!”.

passive.label: passive
passive.plain: The action is done to the subject, and the doer is not named: “it was written” rather than “he wrote”.
passive.short: done to someone, the doer unnamed

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: verbs, subjects and objects

indicative.label: indicative
indicative.plain: The ordinary form of a present-tense verb, for plain statements and questions (usually ending -u), like “he knows”.
indicative.short: the plain present form: a statement

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the subjunctive and jussive moods

subjunctive.label: subjunctive
subjunctive.plain: The form a present-tense verb takes after words like أَنْ “to, that”, لَنْ “will never” and لِـ “so that” (usually ending -a).

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the subjunctive and jussive moods

jussive.label: jussive
jussive.plain: The shortened form a present-tense verb takes after لَمْ “did not”, لَا “do not”, and in “if…” sentences.
jussive.short: the shortened form after “did not / do not / if”

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: the subjunctive and jussive moods

form1.label: form 1
form1.plain: Verb form 1, the pattern فَعَلَ. The basic pattern of a three-letter root: the plain meaning of the action. كَتَبَ “he wrote”; قَالَ “he said”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form2.label: form 2
form2.plain: Verb form 2, the pattern فَعَّلَ. The middle letter is doubled. It often makes the action intensive or makes someone else do it: from عَلِمَ “knew” comes عَلَّمَ “taught”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form3.label: form 3
form3.plain: Verb form 3, the pattern فَاعَلَ. A long ā after the first letter. It often means doing the action with or toward someone: جَاهَدَ “strove (against)”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form4.label: form 4
form4.plain: Verb form 4, the pattern أَفْعَلَ. An a- in front. It often means causing the action: from خَرَجَ “went out” comes أَخْرَجَ “brought out”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form5.label: form 5
form5.plain: Verb form 5, the pattern تَفَعَّلَ. ta- in front and a doubled middle letter. It often means doing form 2’s action to oneself: تَذَكَّرَ “took heed, remembered”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form6.label: form 6
form6.plain: Verb form 6, the pattern تَفَاعَلَ. ta- in front and a long ā. It often means doing the action with each other: تَسَاءَلَ “asked one another”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form7.label: form 7
form7.plain: Verb form 7, the pattern اِنْفَعَلَ. in- in front. It often means the action happening to the subject: اِنْقَلَبَ “turned back, was overturned”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.
form7.short: in- in front: it happens to the subject

form8.label: form 8
form8.plain: Verb form 8, the pattern اِفْتَعَلَ. A t after the first root letter. It often means doing the action for oneself: اِتَّقَىٰ “guarded himself, was mindful”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form9.label: form 9
form9.plain: Verb form 9, the pattern اِفْعَلَّ. A doubled last letter. Used mainly for colours and bodily traits: اِسْوَدَّ “became black”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form10.label: form 10
form10.plain: Verb form 10, the pattern اِسْتَفْعَلَ. ista- in front. It often means asking for the action, or deeming something so: اِسْتَغْفَرَ “asked forgiveness”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

form11.label: form 11
form11.plain: Verb form 11, the pattern اِفْعَالَّ. A long ā and a doubled last letter. A rare, stronger form of form 9 for colours and traits: اِدْهَامَّ “dark green”. Arabic builds related verbs from one root by these patterns; the meanings given are common tendencies, not rules.

root.label: root
root.plain: The core letters, usually three, that carry a basic idea. Many words are built from one root: ك ت ب “writing” gives كَتَبَ “wrote”, كِتَاب “book”, مَكْتُوب “written”.
root.short: the core letters a family of words share

lemma.label: lemma
lemma.plain: The dictionary form of a word: the one entry that all its spellings (with endings, prefixes, he/she/they forms) belong to.
lemma.short: the dictionary form of a word

prefix.label: prefix
prefix.plain: A small word written joined to the front of the next word, such as وَ “and”, بِ “with, in”, لِ “for” or الـ “the”: بِسْمِ = بِ “in” + اسْم “name”.
prefix.short: a small word joined to the front

suffix.label: suffix
suffix.plain: A small word written joined to the end of another, usually a pronoun: كِتَابُهُ “his book” is كِتَاب “book” + هُ “his”.
suffix.short: a small word joined to the end

separate-pronoun.label: Separate pronoun
separate-pronoun.plain: A pronoun written as its own word, not joined to another: هُوَ “he”, أَنْتُمْ “you”.
separate-pronoun.short: a pronoun standing as its own word

possessive.label: Possessive
possessive.plain: A pronoun ending on a noun means “his, her, their, my…”, as in “your Lord”.

object.label: Object
object.plain: A pronoun ending on a verb is usually the one the action is done to, “him, them, us…”, as in “He created you”.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus: verbs, subjects and objects

after-particle.label: After a particle
after-particle.plain: A pronoun ending on a small word: after a preposition it means “him, them, it” (“for him”); after إِنَّ it is the one the sentence is about (“indeed he”).
after-particle.short: on a small word: “for him, indeed he”
